questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -15 \\ 28\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis of the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are $2$ pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. Now, from the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=\frac{3}{5}{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}-2(\frac{3}{5}{x}_{3})=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=\frac{6}{5}{x}_{3}.
$$

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{6}{5}{x}_{3} \\ \frac{3}{5}{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]=\frac{1}{5}{x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{(-10)\cdot 6+(-15)\cdot 3+28\cdot 5}{{6}^{2}+{3}^{2}+{5}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{-60-45+140}{36+9+25}b \\  & =\frac{35}{70}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}6 \\ 3 \\ 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{5}{2}\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Let $u=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -2 \\ 6\end{aligned}]$ and $w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the distance between $u$ and $\text{Span}{w}.$
questions.worked_solution:
The distance between the vector $u$ and the vector space $\text{Span}{w}$ is given by $‖u-\overset{^}{u}‖$, where $\overset{^}{u}$ in the orthogonal projection of $u$ onto $\text{Span}{w}.$ 

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $u$ onto $\text{Span}{w}.$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{w}\,u & =\frac{w\cdot u}{w\cdot w}w \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 4+1\cdot 2+(-2)\cdot (-2)+1\cdot 6}{{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}+(-2)^{2}+{1}^{2}}w \\  & =\frac{8+2+4+6}{4+1+4+1}w \\  & =\frac{20}{10}w \\  & =2w \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -4 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{u}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖u-\overset{^}{u}‖ & =\sqrt{({u}_{1}-{\overset{^}{u}}_{1})^{2}+({u}_{2}-{\overset{^}{u}}_{2})^{2}+({u}_{3}-{\overset{^}{u}}_{3})^{2}+({u}_{4}-{\overset{^}{u}}_{4})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(4-4)^{2}+(2-2)^{2}+(-2-(-4))^{2}+(6-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{0+0+4+16} \\  & =\sqrt{20} \\  & =2\sqrt{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14121442/assets/d887852fe51f08cb7296437e69b6a9632721cfd155558e6abf9a99b4f59f7ad6.png)

First, we find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{a}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{a}\,x & =\frac{a\cdot x}{a\cdot a}a \\  & =\frac{2\cdot 3+3\cdot 7+(-3)(-6)+1\cdot 1}{{2}^{2}+{3}^{2}+(-3)^{2}+{1}^{2}}a \\  & =\frac{6+21+18+1}{4+9+9+1}a \\  & =\frac{46}{23}a \\  & =2a \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ -3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}y & ={\text{proj}}_{a}\,x=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ z & =x-{\text{proj}}_{a}\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 7 \\ -6 \\ 1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 6 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that $y\in \text{Span}{a}$ and $z⊥\text{Span}{a},$ as shown in the picture above.

In conclusion, $z=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ -1\end{aligned}].$

questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -13 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}-3{x}_{3}=0 \\ 2{x}_{1}-{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis of the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 0 \\ 2 & -1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-2{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & -3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 7 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are $2$ pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. Now, from the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=-7{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}-(-7{x}_{3})-3{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=-4{x}_{3}.
$$

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}-4{x}_{3} \\ -7{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -7 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

 

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -7 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{(-10)\cdot (-4)+(-13)\cdot (-7)+1\cdot (1)}{(-4)^{2}+(-7)^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{132}{66}b \\  & =2b \\  & =2[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ -7 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ -14 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given the vector $x$ and the system of linear equations below, find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system.

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}-9 \\ -5 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}-3{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0 \\ {x}_{1}-2{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we need to find a basis of the solution space of the system. 

Consider the augmented matrix $M$ of the system, which we reduce to row echelon form, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}-{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there are $2$ pivot columns ($1$st and $2$nd). Thus, ${x}_{3}$ is a free variable. Now, from the second equation, we get ${x}_{2}=2{x}_{3}.$ Substituting this into the first equation, we obtain 

$$
{x}_{1}-3\cdot (2{x}_{3})+{x}_{3}=0\,⟹\,{x}_{1}=5{x}_{3}.
$$

So, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}5{x}_{3} \\ 2{x}_{3} \\ {x}_{3}\end{aligned}]={x}_{3}[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}\in R.
$$

Consequently, $B={[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}$ is a basis of the solution space of the system.

Finally, we find the projection of $x$ onto the solution space of the system:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{b}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot b}{b\cdot b}b \\  & =\frac{(-9)\cdot 5+(-5)\cdot 2+(-5)\cdot 1}{{5}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}b \\  & =\frac{-60\,}{\,\,\,30\,}b \\  & =-2b \\  & =-2[\begin{aligned}5 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-10 \\ -4 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$
